nodes.title: MCP-ecosystem advisory corpus 2025-06..2026-10: 58 dated advisories analysed (66 pulled via gh api from 10 repos + 13 ToolHive/other)
nodes.summary: Each row: GHSA, CVE where assigned, date, root cause, one-sentence invariant, structural-prevention verdict (T=type/capability boundary, S=statelessness, N=neither), conformance case id. Classes: A origin/DNS-rebind 15, B session/principal 7, C audience 2, D OAuth mix-up/SSRF 6, E redirect leak 4, F unbounded state 8, G parser differential/policy 8, H gateway-specific 8.
nodes.overclaim_risk: Counts are of advisories I read, not of all MCP vulns; 66 are gh-api primary, ToolHive entries partially from advisory titles
nodes.underclaim_risk: Many advisories not in these repos (ruby/kotlin/php SDKs, litellm, context-forge, microsoft/mcp-gateway) only skimmed

nodes.title: Same default-off DNS-rebinding bug filed independently in TS, Python, Go, Java, rmcp, Docker gateway, Ruby within 2025-12..2026-04
nodes.summary: Opt-in security = recurring advisory. Also TS shared-instance cross-delivery recurred (GHSA-345p then GHSA-jm63), agentgateway OpenAPI traversal fixed twice 7 months apart (v0.12.0 CVE-2026-29791 -> v1.6.0 GHSA-h7hp), rmcp SSRF filter fixed incompletely (c9xm -> 5p52). Fix-twice rate is evidence that a regression corpus is needed.

nodes.title: Statelessness removes session-confusion class but not Origin, parser, audience, or SSRF classes; it creates new ones
nodes.summary: Of 58 advisories, S-verdict only on class B and F-state items (~8); Java GHSA-hp8w showed default stateless transport lost the accidental session CSRF barrier; ToolHive GHSA-7h6f showed the 2026-07-28 path skipped Host check. MRTR requestState moves state to client: spec says attacker-controlled, MUST integrity-protect; sealing is default-on in Python (PR #3032) but opt-in feature `request-state` in rmcp and opt-in in TS.
nodes.overclaim_risk: Verdict S/T is my judgement, not primary
nodes.underclaim_risk: Contrarian view: stateless makes B-class removable

nodes.title: Spec 2026-07-28 streamable-http: 'If Origin header is present and invalid -> 403' leaves absent Origin accepted
nodes.summary: Matches Inspector GHSA-wmjf-2m46-2352 and docker CVE-2026-76092 originSecurityHandler allowing no-Origin. Non-browser clients legitimately omit Origin, so rule must be credential-conditioned: absent Origin OK only with bearer/mTLS credential, never with ambient auth (cookies, loopback trust).
nodes.overclaim_risk: Read of spec tag text by me at 2026-10; not re-quoted verbatim in this node

nodes.title: Secure-default vs usability: Go PR #842 default CrossOriginProtection (2026-03-13) reverted by PR #906 (2026-04-24, fixes #902) after github-mcp-server browser clients broke
nodes.summary: Contrarian: defaults get reverted. Gateway must expose typed explicit opt-out rather than silent default-off.

nodes.title: Invariant list ranked by advisories prevented (of 58)
nodes.summary: 1. Outbound fetches checked on resolved connected address; redirects strip credentials cross-origin (18); 2. Listener gate: Host allowlist + Origin allowlist (absent Origin treated per credential) + Content-Type application/json, applied at the listener for every route and protocol revision (15); 3. One strict parser shared by policy and backend: reject duplicate/case-variant/NUL/BOM keys; policy evaluates only fully parsed names, unparseable denies (8); 4. Token aud == this resource server, enforced non-optionally; OAuth credentials only to pinned issuer; PRM resource must match (8); 5. Pre-auth and per-request memory bounded: body cap, batch cap, session TTL, no unbounded caches (8); 6. Listener cannot be constructed without authenticator; defaults secure (signature verify, audience) with typed opt-out (8); 7. Principal scoping: every stateful handle (session, task, requestState, response route) is bound to authenticated principal and scope; lookup outside scope returns 404 (7)
nodes.overclaim_risk: Ranking depends on my class assignment and counts duplicates of one bug across SDKs as separate advisories (that is the point: they recur)
nodes.underclaim_risk: Counts understate: single advisory may break several invariants

nodes.title: Origin / audience / session rule set for AEGIS listener
nodes.summary: 1) Host in allowlist else 403 (HTTP/1.1 Host and H2 :authority both). 2) Origin present and not allowlisted -> 403; Origin absent allowed only if request carries bearer or mTLS credential. 3) POST Content-Type must be application/json else 415. 4) No ACAO wildcard; preflight only for allowlisted origins. 5) Token aud == canonical resource URI, mandatory, no opt-out in release builds. 6) Any state handle (Mcp-Session-Id if accepted for legacy, task id, requestState, SSE stream) carries (principal, route, backend, policy-version, ttl) and is sealed (AEAD); mismatch -> 404. 7) Under 2026-07-28 no session minting; requestState sealed by default (not opt-in). 8) Rules live in listener type so every protocol revision route inherits them (ToolHive 7h6f). 9) Strict JSON parse shared with policy engine; unparseable -> deny. 10) Egress: resolved-address check at connect, redirects stripped cross-origin, args never from untrusted metadata.
nodes.overclaim_risk: Rule 2 absent-Origin conditioning is my design, not tested against real clients
nodes.underclaim_risk: Rule 7 default-sealing may be unnecessary if no handler uses requestState
